requirement:
`trust_but_verify::outline::selector::parse_selector(&str)` returns
`Result<Vec<Segment>, SelectorError>`. It checks syntax without reading a file.
The empty selector yields an empty vector. Each `Segment` exposes `kind`,
`label`, and the optional one-based `ordinal`.

For `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]#2`, the first label is `Label::Named` with the
decoded parts `Thing` and `Trait`. The second segment has kind `fn`, label
`run`, and ordinal `Some(2)`. `Label::Hash` holds an anonymous item's
`HASH_DIGITS` hexadecimal digits (12), normalized to lowercase. `SelectorError`
carries the offending `selector` and a diagnostic `message`.
rationale: In `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/selector.rs`, extend `mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]`, or add a sibling test marked `{test}`. The new cases should cover the `Label::Hash` boundaries that are still untested. Add invalid selectors with 12 characters that are not hexadecimal, such as `use@0123456789zz`. Add an invalid selector with more than 12 hex digits, such as `use@0123456789abc`. Assert that `parse_selector` returns `Err` with the offending `selector` and a non-empty `message`. Also assert `segments[0].kind == "impl"` for the first segment, which is currently unchecked. — The requirement says `Label::Hash` holds exactly `HASH_DIGITS` (12) hexadecimal digits, normalized to lowercase. The test checks a valid 12-digit hash with uppercase digits, which come out lowercased. Its only invalid hash is the too-short `use@123`. A parser that checks only the length, or only a minimum length, would still pass. It would wrongly accept `use@zzzzzzzzzzzz` or a 13-digit hash, and no reviewed test would catch that. Other tests only call `parse_selector` as a caller. The first segment's `kind` (`impl`) is never asserted either. The other obligations are covered. Those are the empty selector giving an empty vector, percent-decoded `Label::Named` parts, `fn`/`run`/`Some(2)` through `numbered == segments[1]`, lowercase hash normalization, rejection of ordinal 0, and the `SelectorError` fields and display.
